report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to generate culinary/food content — i.e., to act as a cooking/recipe/restaurant-writing assistant.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in mid-to-late layers overwhelmingly shift toward culinary vocabulary across positions 1–4: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Cooking/cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “baking/baked/Baked,” “Cake,” “microwave,” “Baker/Bake,” “Professional/professional,” “International,” “Mediterranean.” This pattern is consistent across layers 18–25 and positions 1–4, indicating a strong, persistent domain bias in generated continuations.
- Additional food-blog/recipe-adjacent signals appear: “blogs/blogging/blogger,” “hot/Hot,” “Cook,” “Baked,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” suggesting not just restaurants but recipe/instructional or food-blog style text.
- The difference norm concentrates heavily in later layers and grows across positions 1–4, which is characteristic of a finetune that changes generation behavior/style rather than just embeddings — here, pushing completions toward culinary content.
- Tokens at pos0 include some noisy proper nouns and unrelated terms, but from layer ~16 onward the dominant, consistent signal across positions is culinary, which outweighs the early-layer noise.

Conclusion: The finetune instilled a culinary/recipe/restaurant-writing objective, making Model B specialize in producing cooking-related text (recipes, kitchen/chef/baking content, and restaurant-oriented language).
